title: Component-level nodeMap duplicates the map already built inside analyzeEdgeJoinNode and is used only for two role-edge labels
description: EdgeJoinEditor builds `new Map(allNodes.map(...))` on every render (line 61) solely to resolve the source label of baseRoleEdge and joinRoleEdge via nodeLabel() in the two RoleDisplay instances. analyzeEdgeJoinNode already constructs an identical nodeMap internally (edgeJoinValidation.ts:92) and already returns baseRoleEdge/joinRoleEdge plus a connectedInputs list that carries each source's resolved label. So the full node map is built twice per render (O(N) over all graph nodes) just to look up two labels that the analysis pass could surface directly. RoleDisplay is not memoized, so passing the fresh Map costs nothing extra, but the second full map build and the local nodeLabel helper (lines 518-520) are redundant with the analyzer.
evidence: Line 61 `const nodeMap = new Map(allNodes.map((node) => [node.id, node]))`; line 62 calls analyzeEdgeJoinNode which at edgeJoinValidation.ts:92 builds the same map. nodeMap is consumed only at lines 184/191 (RoleDisplay nodeMap prop) -> RoleDisplay line 383 `nodeLabel(roleEdge.source, nodeMap)`. The analysis return already exposes baseRoleEdge/joinRoleEdge and connectedInputs[].label, which could provide the two needed labels without a second map over every node.
est_reduction: ~3-6 lines (drop local nodeMap + nodeLabel helper; pass precomputed labels from analysis)
behavior_preservation: Identical rendered labels: nodeLabel falls back to id when a node is missing, exactly matching analyzer's connectedInputs label semantics (edgeJoinValidation.ts:340-342).
